items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: I never did know what his last name was. He was telling me about all these records that Stanley had down there.

ctx.x: the guy who I guess was the maintenance man of the apartment building lived in the basement. He was also an amateur electrician, he fixed things for people. And this fellow, George McIver, used to tell me about this fellow, the maintenance man -- his name was Stanley; I never did know what his last name was. He was telling me about all these records that Stanley had down there. He said, "You ought to hear a record of a guy down there that's he's playing named Art Tatum."

He took me over one time and he played this record for me. The first thing I heard of Art Tatum was a thing I never will forget -- it was called "Emeline". It was "Emeline," there's another one called "Moonglow," and another one called "Beautiful Love." I don't remember exactly what the other one was. I think it was "I Could Do Most Anything For You," but I'm not sure. Anyway, this just floored me. I just didn't believe nobody could make a piano sound like that. As a matter of fact, it was just like listening to…
